title: Inference All-Hands — Field Notes, Risks & Action Items (Oct 12 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
We ran a cross-org inference all-hands to sync on production signal, recent incidents, rollout readiness for model-variant-routing v2, and a short list of engineering priorities through the end of Q4. This doc captures the verbal notes, explicit risks surfaced, and concrete action items (owners + rough ETA). Treat as the canonical follow-up for the next two weeks.

Attendees (summary):
- Engineering leadership: Alyssa Chen (owner), Marcus Klein
- Serving runtime: Priya Patel, Samir Gupta
- Platform engineering: Leah O'Neill, Diego Morales
- Observability: Noor Shah (joined late)
- SRE: Jason Park
- Product & PM: Mira Santos
- Solutions & Svc Eng: Rowan Li

Top-line metrics shared:
- P95 token latency (hosted clusters) increased from 420ms to 520ms (week-over-week) on short sequences (<=128 toks) during peak (US-PAC region).
- Average tokens/sec per GPU has fallen ~9% after kernel upgrade 3.1.2 on some nvlink host types.
- Error budget burn rate spiked to 1.6x baseline during the staged canary on Oct 9 (region failovers and a cascading retry storm).
- Cache hit rate for prefix caching: 27% (target 40% for our conversational workloads).

Observed causes and hypotheses discussed:
1) Kernel upgrade 3.1.2: changed scheduling behavior for small-batch workloads; microbenchmarks show improved throughput for long sequences but regressions for short sequences hitting many concurrent tiny contexts. (Priya lead).
2) Smart-routing weight adjustments: a conservative routing tweak sent 18% more traffic to dedicated clusters with slightly different quantization profiles, exposing mismatch latency behaviors. (Leah/FM note).
3) KV cache eviction policy across autoscaling events: warm cache pages lost during node churn due to scale-down windows being too aggressive; rebuilt cache thrash caused extra upstream work. (Samir/Jason).
4) Observability blind spot: some CDN edge retries were not surfaced in our per-request tracing (missing span in legacy tracing shim). (Noor).

Decisions made during meeting:
- Rollback of kernel 3.1.2 on host pool rpcc-2 for the short-term canary. Ops to run rollback windows tonight (Jason).
- Freeze smart-routing weight changes until we have a predictive simulator to estimate latency impact for mixed quantization fleets. Product approved.
- Retro-fit TTL-aware cache draining to reduce eviction-induced rebuilds during scale-downs (Samir to own design).

Concrete action items (owner — ETA):
- Immediate rollback of kernel 3.1.2 on rpcc-2 canary hosts (Jason Park — 2026-10-12 EOD).
- Run controlled microbench suite across sequence length buckets (1-32, 33-128, 129-512) to isolate kernel regression surface and publish a short report (Priya Patel — 2026-10-14).
- Add per-request CDN retry span to tracing shim and backfill last 72 hours of logs for correlation (Noor Shah — 2026-10-18).
- Implement TTL-aware cache draining plan: design doc + perf targets (Samir Gupta — draft 2026-10-19, implementation kickoff 2026-10-25).
- Build a small traffic simulator for routing weight experiments: prototype sampling-based estimator to predict p95 shifts (Leah O'Neill + Platform Eng — prototype 2026-10-21).
- Post-mortem for Oct 9 canary incident capturing timeline, decisions, and missed alarms (Jason & Priya — post-mortem published 2026-10-15).

Risks and mitigations called out:
- Risk: Repeated rollbacks increase operational churn and make it harder to iterate. Mitigation: adopt staggered rollout windows and add automated rollback criteria (SLO-based). (Marcus to draft SLO rollback playbook — 2026-10-20).
- Risk: If cache warm-up remains low, unit costs rise substantially under bursty workloads. Mitigation: tune autoscaler to prefer scale-up headroom over aggressive scale-down during peak windows; invest in proactive cache pre-warming for predictable customer cohorts. (Samir + Solutions Eng — plan by 2026-10-26).
- Risk: Blind spots in tracing hide important failure modes. Mitigation: extend observability contract and run two-week audit of spans across the ingress path. (Noor — audit completed 2026-10-25).

Requests for other teams:
- Product: hold routing weight adjustments until simulator shows <3% p95 delta for top-10 customers.
- Solutions Eng: provide top-5 customer traffic patterns for targeted cache pre-warm testing (Rowan Li).
- Security/Compliance: confirm that rollback and probing experiments do not require additional approvals for a subset of customers in EU-PAC region (Alyssa to loop in legal).

Open questions we couldn't resolve in meeting:
- How much of the latency delta is due to quantization profile mismatch vs kernel scheduling? (blocked until Priya's microbench).
- Can we safely extend scale-down grace window in Dedicated without impacting cost commitments? (finance tradeoff; ops/finance sync needed).

Follow-ups and check-ins:
- Quick sync: Ops + SRE status check tomorrow 09:30 PT to confirm rollback and initial telemetry.
- Deep-dive: microbench review and draft recommendations next Wednesday 11:00 PT (Priya lead).
- Two-week progress review in next all-hands (tentatively Oct 26) to validate the risk list has reduced and action items are on-track.

Appendix (notes captured live):
- Mira: "Customers on Dedicated reported subtle flakiness around 10/8; not full outages but higher error rates on long-poll endpoints."
- Jason: "We saw a retry storm that correlated with an internal throttling rule firing after a cascade of 429s."
- Priya: "Initial kernel telemetry suggests the scheduler added a micro-yielding path that increases context-switch overhead for many tiny seqs — working with vendors."
- Leah: "Platform will hold off the routing roll beyond the 20% gradual step we had planned; we'll add a traffic shadow run instead."

If you were in the meeting, please add any missing notes or correct owners. If you were assigned an action item, add an issue to Linear and tag this doc in the issue body.

End of notes.
